paragraph: Single-family is the Paramus market, with 105 sales over six months at a median of $1,085,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.00. Slightly under half sold above asking with a median of 21 days on market, which is competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes are moving, and sellers are getting their number without giving much away. Sales ran from $625,000 to $3,500,000, so the median is the better guide than any single comparable. Condos and townhouses are a small but distinctly upper-end tier here, 19 sales at a median of $1,700,000, above the single-family median. That isn't the entry-level category some buyers expect it to be. Median days on market was 5, though only 3 of 19 went above asking, so speed is coming from product that's spoken for rather than bidding wars. Co-op activity was 4 sales at a median of $356,250, too thin to read as a trend. Monthly volume climbed steadily from 12 single-family closings in February to 26 in July while the median bounced between $910,000 and $1,650,000. That swing is mix, not values moving. If Paramus follows the usual seasonal arc, expect volume and medians to ease through fall.
